title: How To Calm And Reset Your Classroom
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that a teacher's temperament transfers to students and that calm, controlled energy should govern most of the school day, reserving enthusiasm for directed lessons. He then offers a specific reset strategy for when tension has already built up and students are antsy, irritable, or unfocused: one minute of scheduled silence devoted to slow diaphragmatic breathing, framed to students explicitly as a mutual benefit rather than a punishment. He walks through the mechanics — sitting up straight, breathing in and out through the nose from the diaphragm, counting four-to-six-second inhales and exhales — and explains the physiological basis, that slower breathing triggers the parasympathetic nervous system's calming response. He recommends scheduling it at predictable high-tension points like mid-morning, after lunch, or before dismissal, arguing that with repetition it becomes something students come to look forward to as a calming reset.
points: Save enthusiastic, kinetic energy for directed lessons; keep transitions and general instruction as calm as a zen garden.
